findings.title: Return to the governing and formative source
findings.claim: The focus return is more than relocation: the governed person is brought back to the Lord as owner and authority, while the destination also carries the possibility of formative completion.
findings.mechanism: The focus occurrences of رَبِّكَ and الرُّجْعَىٰٓ supply the governed endpoint and ordinary return carrier. Independent wider connections join return to God, restoration under effective power, and return to the Lord with acceptance, making authority, source, and completion meet in one bounded reading.
findings.reader_payoff: The destination phrase can be perceived as reattachment to the authority that governs the returned person, not merely as movement toward an abstract place.
findings.containment: The ordinary destination reading remains primary. The wider target records do not supply target morphology, and the formative relation is a qualified contextual resonance rather than a claim that every return formula means nurture or completion.

epistemic.reason: The finding has trusted focus-anchored support, but its wider connection targets lack supplied morphology and therefore qualify the contextual extensions.

findings.title: Return as a returned answer
findings.claim: The focus return can include an answer sent back to the one who issued a command or question, so conduct becomes a form of response.
findings.mechanism: The focus noun الرُّجْعَىٰٓ carries the returned-response branch. Independent connections place return to God inside a call-and-response setting and describe mutual return of speech, allowing the directional return relation to contact an answer sent back through speech or conduct.
findings.reader_payoff: Commands and questions in the wider field can be felt as requiring an answer that comes back through the person's response, not only as statements preceding a final destination.
findings.containment: This is a qualified contextual extension of the destination reading. The wider targets lack supplied morphology, and the answer relation does not replace the focus noun's ordinary return or assert that the return is only verbal.

epistemic.reason: Trusted focus-anchored support is reinforced by concrete speech-return connections, while unsupplied target morphology limits the strength of the cross-ayah extension.
